title: Capability announcement prefix encoding: vector pins 16-byte prefix for /64, Python requires prefix_len/8 bytes
description: Found wiring test/vectors/capability_announcements.json. capability_prefix_delegation and capability_both pin prefix=fd000000000000000000000000000000 (16 bytes) with prefix_len=64, but python/src/lichen/crypto/capability_announcements.py CapabilityPayload enforces prefix length == prefix_len/8 (8 bytes for /64) and raises ValueError('prefix must be 8 bytes for prefix_len 64, got 16') at decode. The vectors were generated by the independent reference oracle, so both sides are internally consistent - this needs a spec ruling (spec section 8.12 / 08-gateway-coordination.md): is the on-wire prefix field truncated to prefix_len bits (compact) or always 128-bit? Whichever side loses must be regenerated. Related layering notes from the same wiring session: reserved-bits and kid-vs-announcer_iid checks fire at DECODE level in Python while the vectors expect verify-level detection (net decision identical: invalid); invalid_reserved_bits pins capabilities=255 which Python cannot even construct. Consumer documents these as _DECODE_REJECT cases in python/tests/crypto/test_orphan_vector_consumers.py.
close_reason: Decided: compact encoding (prefix_len/8 bytes) per spec 06-security.md line 914. Python is correct. Vectors need regeneration with 8-byte prefix for /64. Filed as agent-workable fix.
